AWPTCM-T33241.objective:
• A loopback interface can be created, enabled, assigned an IP address (IPv4 and IPv6), and remains in the Up state by definition.
  • Traffic sent to a loopback interface IP address is processed locally by the device.
  • Multiple loopback interfaces can coexist on the same device.
  • A loopback interface with an assigned IP address remains operational and reachable after stack failover and normal reloads.
  • A loopback interface can be disabled and deleted.
  • Loopback interface IP addresses can be used as stable source addresses for syslog, SNMP, RIP, OSPF, and BGP.
  • Configuration limits for the number of loopback interfaces and primary IP addresses per interface are enforced.
  • The Loopback interface state and assigned addresses are correctly reported by show commands.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability
Create a loopback interface, assign an IPv4 and IPv6 address, and verify it is Up by definition and traffic to the address is processed locally.
Create multiple loopback interfaces. Confirm they coexist and each can be assigned addresses independently.
Configure a loopback interface with an IP address, then perform stack failover and normal reload. Verify the loopback remains operational and reachable afterward.
Disable and delete a loopback interface. Confirm correct behavior.
Configure a loopback interface IP as the source for syslog, SNMP, RIP, OSPF, and BGP. Verify it functions correctly as a stable source address.
Test configuration limits for the number of loopback interfaces and primary addresses per interface.
Verify that show commands correctly report the Loopback state and assigned IP addresses.
